commits.messageBody:
The condition counter counts every "catch", "if", "for", "while" and
"case" token, also when it is the name of a member:

    function load(p) {
      return p.then(parse).catch(() => null);
    }

The cyclomatic complexity of load is 2 instead of 1: every
promise.catch(f) adds one, as a catch clause does, and so do o.if,
o.for, o.while and o.case.

A keyword right after "." or "?." is the name of a member; the
TypeScript reader, which JavaScript, JSX and TSX use, now takes back
the condition counted for it, as the Swift reader does for its optional
marker. The nested structures (-ENS) still count such a "catch": that
extension does not depend on the language reader.
commits.messageHeadline: Do not count a JavaScript member named as a keyword as a condition

title: Do not count a JavaScript member named as a keyword as a condition
